description:
src/methods/mod.rs:242-253: `pub(crate) fn session_parts(&self) -> Result<(&str, &str), ClientError>`. Both returned slices borrow from `self.session`.

Every call site is:
```
let (api_url, account_id) = self.session_parts()?;
let args = json!({"accountId": account_id, ...});  // borrows account_id
let req = build_request(...);                        // moves args
let resp = self.call_internal(api_url, &req).await?; // holds api_url across await
```

`api_url` is borrowed across an .await point. This works because `SessionClient: !Sync` is implicit and the future borrows `&self` for its full lifetime. But the moment a caller wants to drive multiple `session_parts()` results concurrently or store one in a struct, the lifetime tie to `&self` becomes a problem.

Idiomatic alternative: return owned `(String, Id)` — small allocation, clears the lifetime. Or split into `api_url(&self) -> &str` + `primary_account_id(&self) -> Result<&str, ClientError>` so callers know which lives where.

Lower priority because it works and has no current bug; flag is for future-self when async pipelining gets requested.
title: session_parts() returns &str pair — caller cannot store the result across an await
